runs.t: •  Ask: How much is this shirt?

slides.notes:
Welcome. Say: "Today: money and clothes." Point to the price tag: "How much is it? It's $25."
Bring 2 or 3 real clothes you can hold up (a shirt or a jacket, a pair of shoes), and put one far away on a chair (for that / those).
Before class: print the play-money page (one per pair), cut it, and put each pair's money in an envelope.
Money is private. Use only play money and the prices on the pages. Never ask what learners earn, spend, or pay.
Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Say less, show more.
Class plan: 6:00 Hello + Review, 6:10 New Words, 6:20 Listening, 6:32 Grammar, 6:45 Break, 7:00 Talk Time, 7:10 Exit Ticket + Homework, 7:15 Letters & Numbers, 7:25 Progress Check.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (At a glance, How to Use This Plan, Clock-time plan).

slides.title: How Much Is It?

runs.t: I can use this, that, these, those.
I can say a blue shirt, black shoes.
I can pay and check my change.

slides.notes:
Click to show each goal, one at a time. Read it aloud. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: hold up a shirt. "How much is this shirt?" Goal 2: "It's $12." Say "twelve dollars".
Goal 3: this / that = one thing; these / those = two or more. Near = this / these. Far = that / those.
Goal 4: the color comes before the thing: a blue shirt, black shoes.
Goal 5: "Cash or credit card? Cash, please. Here's $20. Your change is $5."
Letters & Numbers at 7:15: reading prices ($4.99 = "four ninety-nine"), this / these sounds, and a receipt.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (At a glance: Objectives).
slides.title: Today's Goals

runs.t: A: Is the store open on Sunday?

slides.notes:
Pairs. Review of last week (time and days). 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
Before class, write on the board: What time is it? What time is class? What day is class? Is the store open on Sunday?
Model with one learner: "What time is it?" "It's six o'clock." "What day is class?" "It's on Monday."
Click to show the A question. Click again for the B answers. Partners switch, then find a new partner. Help: "Can you repeat, please?" "How do you spell it?"
Last 3 minutes: homework check. Partners show each other the Lesson 6 homework. Look at item 2 (at / on / in).
New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can do the Lesson 1–6 Progress Checks at home. If behind: one partner only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Step 1: Hello + Review; Student Pages: Hello + Review).

slides.notes:

cash: show the play money. credit card: mime paying with a card.
Write on the board: 100 cents = 1 dollar (100¢ = $1).

pants, shoes: say "pants" and hold up 2 fingers. One thing, but the word is always plural.
colors: red, blue, black, white, green, yellow.
Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then A says a color, B points to something in the room with that color.

runs.t: Ana is at a clothing store.
Can I have the receipt, please?

slides.notes:
Before you listen (1 min). Say: "Ana is at a clothing store. She asks: How much is it?" Point to the shirts and shoes in Task A.
Click to show each listen. Listen 1: Task A (circle the shirt and the shoes). Listen 2: Task B (write the 2 prices). Listen 3: Task C (check the total, cash or card, and write the change).
Say it!: read each line. Learners repeat.
The audio L1_L7_listening.mp3 (about 1:10) plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen. Pairs compare after each task.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Say the prices as words: twelve dollars, thirty dollars.

runs.t: B: the prices.  C: check or write.
Asks for: a bag   the receipt

slides.notes:
Listen 2 (Task B): learners write the 2 prices. Listen 3 (Task C): learners check the total, cash or card, and write the change.
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer.
Task B: 1 the shirt is $12, 2 the shoes are $30.

slides.title: Listening B + C

slides.notes:
Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
Box 1: hold up the shirt: "How much is this shirt?" Click: "It's $12." Box 2: hold up the shoes: "How much are these shoes?" Click: "They're $30."
Click to show each answer. Learners repeat the question and the answer.
Write on the board: one → is / it's. two or more → are / they're. Pants and shoes always use are.
Say prices as words: $12 = "twelve dollars". Not "How much cost this?"
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Boxes 1–2; Grammar Boxes 1 and 2; Teacher notes).

slides.title: How much is it?

runs.t: Two or more: near or far?

slides.notes:
Box 3 (the key point). Stand next to the shirt: "this shirt." Walk away and point to the far chair: "that shirt."
Same with shoes: "these shoes… those shoes." Learners point near and far as they say the words.
Ask "One thing: near or far?" Click to show this shirt / that shirt. Ask "Two or more?" Click to show these shoes / those shoes.
One thing → is / this / that. Two or more → are / these / those. Near → this / these. Far → that / those.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 3; Grammar Box 3; Teacher notes).
Pictures: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized, recolored, and combined with drawn parts (see lesson7/images/CREDITS.md). Near / far lines and labels are drawn in code.
slides.title: this, that, these, those

slides.notes:
Box 4: write a shirt blue on the board and cross it out. Write a blue shirt. Then black shoes (yes) and blacks shoes (no): colors never take -s.
Read each DON'T SAY line. Shake your head. Click to show the SAY line. Learners repeat it.
The big mistake this week: Spanish says una camisa azul. In English the color comes first: a blue shirt. Correct by pointing at the word order on the board. Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page.
Check question: "shirt / red / a" (a red shirt).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 4; Grammar Box 4; Teacher notes).
slides.title: Color + Noun

runs.t: Thank you. Can I have the receipt, please?

slides.notes:
Box 5: model paying with play money: "That's $8." Give $10. "Your change is $2."
Read the cashier line: "That's $42. Cash or credit card?" Click: "Cash, please. Here's $50." Another answer: "Credit card, please."
Right box: "Your change is $8." Click: "Thank you. Can I have the receipt, please?"
Pairs: A is the cashier, B is the shopper. Then switch. Use the play money.
Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A points to a picture on the New Words page and asks; B invents a price. Then switch. If behind: skip the pair drill; it becomes homework.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 5 and pair drill; Grammar Box 5).

slides.title: Grammar Box 5

runs.t: Write is, are, this, or these.
Then put the words in order.

slides.notes:
Learners write is, are, this, or these on lines 1–4, and put the words in order on line 5. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer: 1 is, 2 are, 3 this, 4 these, 5 a red shirt.
Say: "One thing: is, this. Two or more: are, these." Pants always use are.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Grammar: Practice; Answer key, Grammar practice).
slides.title: is, are, this, these?

slides.notes:
Read each "Don't say" line. Shake your head. Click to show the correct line. Learners repeat it.
is / are: one thing → How much is this shirt? Two or more → How much are these shoes? Not "How much cost this?"
The color comes first: a blue shirt. Colors never take -s: black shoes, not blacks shoes.
this shoes → these shoes: shoes are two or more.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Grammar: Common mistakes; Teacher notes).

shapes.name: Play money picture
shapes.alt: play money: $1, $5, $10, $20 bills and coins, marked PLAY MONEY

runs.t: How much is this red dress?

slides.notes:
A–B pairs. Give half the class the Student A page and half the Student B page, and each pair one envelope of play money. Partners don't show their pages.
Model with one learner (you are the shopper): point to the dress. "How much is this red dress?" "It's $25." "OK. Here's $30." "Your change is $5." Write the price and the change on the board.
Click to show each step. Part 1 (4 min): A is the cashier (Store 1, with prices). B is the shopper: B gets the play money, asks the price of the 3 things, writes the prices, buys one thing, pays, and checks the change.
Answer key, Store 1: red dress $25, black pants $18, white shoes $35.
With an odd number, two Bs share one A (one is the shopper, one helps count the money). Learners who can't read or write yet are good cashiers: they say the price from the tag and count the play money.
Play money only, never real money.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Step 5: Talk Time; Student Pages: Talk Time A and B, Play Money; Answer key).
Pictures: drawn in code for this curriculum, no outside source (see lesson7/images/CREDITS.md). The play money is marked PLAY MONEY and does not copy any real bill or coin.
slides.title: Talk Time

runs.t: A: How much is this green jacket?

slides.notes:
Part 2 (4 min): switch. B is the cashier (Store 2). A is the shopper.
Model it: "How much is this green jacket?" Click: "It's $40."
A asks the prices, writes them, buys one thing, pays, and checks the change: "Here's $___. My change is $___."
Answer key, Store 2: green jacket $40, yellow shirt $9, blue pants $22.
Check (2 min): partners show their pages. Are the prices the same?
Fast pairs: buy 2 things and say the total: "That's $43." Strong learners can add: "Do you have this in ___?" New learners use only "How much is this?" and point.
If behind: one round only (Part 1). Collect the play money at the end.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 2, Check, Fast pairs; Answer key; Teacher notes).
slides.title: Store 2: Switch

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): hold up a picture or a real item. Each learner asks "How much is this ___?" / "How much are these ___?" or writes one color + noun (a red dress). Copying is fine.
Homework (10 minutes): open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first line). Point to each instruction.
Homework: 1) write is or are; 2) put the words in order; 3) look at 3 price tags in a store (or in an ad) and write them; 4) say the prices to a family member or a friend: "It's four ninety-nine."; 5) review: English class is on ___, at ___.
Homework answers: item 1: 1 is, 2 are, 3 are, 4 is. Item 2: 1 a green jacket, 2 black shoes, 3 a white dress.
Collect the play money for next time.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Step 6: Exit Ticket + Homework; Student Pages: Homework; Answer key).

slides.title: Before You Go

slides.notes:
Letters & Numbers (10 min). Whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page.
Task A, see it (2 min): point to each price and say it. Learners repeat. Click to show each way to say it.
$4.99 = "four ninety-nine"; $12.50 = "twelve fifty"; $20.00 = "twenty dollars"; $0.25 = "twenty-five cents". People don't say the word dollars or cents in $4.99.
The dot is a period; the numbers after it are cents.
Partners: A says a price from Task A, B points to it. Switch.
Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the prices with everyone and point.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Letters & Numbers, Task A; Teacher notes: Saying prices).
slides.title: Say the Prices

slides.notes:
Task B, hear it (2 min). Say each price 2 times: 1 $4.99 ("four ninety-nine"), 2 $13 ("thirteen dollars"), 3 $15.50 ("fifteen fifty"), 4 $60 ("sixty dollars"), 5 $2.25 ("two twenty-five"). Learners circle.
Then click to show each answer.
-teen / -ty matter again: $13 or $30? Say "thir-TEEN" and "THIR-ty" with a clap.
If behind: do Tasks A and B only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Letters & Numbers, Task B; Answer key, Letters & Numbers Task B; Teacher notes).
slides.title: Circle the Price

slides.notes:
Task C, say it (2 min): this has a short i (like six); these has a long ee (like three). Smile wide for ee.
Click to show each group. Say the pairs; learners repeat: this shirt / these shoes, it is / they're green, six / three.
Many learners say this and these the same. Don't over-correct; the grammar (is / are) helps listeners understand.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Letters & Numbers, Task C; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Read the Receipt

slides.notes:
Progress Check (5 min). Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read the 5 prices slowly, 2 times each: 1 $12, 2 $40, 3 $5.99 ("five ninety-nine"), 4 $18, 5 $70. Learners circle.
Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Help with the instructions only. Click to show the Part B answers when you check together: 1 c, 2 a, 3 d, 4 b.
Part C answers: 1 are, 2 is, 3 a red dress.
Part D: read each "I can…" line and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Part A shows who can hear prices (and -teen / -ty); Part C shows is / are and color + noun. Collect the pages.
Week 8 is the midterm. If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 8 at 6:00, before the midterm.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson7/Level1_Lesson7.md (Progress Check; Answer key).
